sentences.text: This appeal is filed by the claimant in O.P (MV) No.1497 of 2014 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Irinjalakuda.
The respondent herein is the second respondent before the tribunal.

2. According to the claimant, on 17.11.2014 at about 07.45 am, while the claimant was riding a motorcycle bearing registration no. KL-45-F-5540 through Chilanka Pakarappilly road, another motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-32-F-9947 driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit against the appellant.
As a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
The appellant approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 10,25,000/- limited to 5,00,000/-.
3. The first respondent, who is the owner cum driver of the offending vehicle, remained ex parte before the Tribunal.
The second respondent insurer filed a written statement admitting the insurance policy, but disputing the quantum of compensation claimed.
Before the tribunal, Exts.A1 to A13 were marked.

The MACA NO. 3397 OF 2017 2025:KER:66565 tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, awarded a sum of 1,24,600/- as compensation under different heads with interest @9% per annum from the date of petition till realization with proportionate costs against the second respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant has come up in appeal.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned Standing Counsel for the respondent insurance company.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant claims enhancement mainly under the following heads :-
Notional income :-

The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that, at the time of the accident, the appellant was employed as a Physical Education Teacher in a private school and was earning a monthly salary of 16,000/.

The learned counsel relied on Ext.A10 salary certificate issued by the school authorities, which shows that,
as on 07.04.2015, the appellant was working as a Physical Education Teacher and was drawing a monthly salary of 16,000/-.
On a perusal of Ext.A13 Degree Certificate, it is seen that the certificate was issued on 05.03.2016 MACA NO. 3397 OF 2017 2025:KER:66565 and that he had passed the Degree Examination in April 2015.
Hence, it is evident that, as on the date of the accident ie; on 17.11.2014, he was not a graduate in Physical Education.

On the other hand, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that Ext.A10 certificate has not been proved by examining the employer, and moreover, since the certificate was issued in 2015, the salary stated therein cannot be accepted.
However, as per Ext.A10 certificate, it is seen that he was working as a Physical Education Teacher in the afore school.

Considering the afore facts, I find that the income fixed by the tribunal is on the lower side and in order to award a just and reasonable compensation, I find it appropriate to re-fix the income at 12,000/-.

2 Loss of earnings :-

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that Ext.A10 salary certificate reveals that he had loss of pay for nearly two months.
On a perusal of the award, it is evident that the Tribunal considered only a period of two months for the purpose of awarding compensation under the said head.

As per Ext.A3 wound certificate, the appellant sustained the following injuries:
MACA NO. 3397 OF 2017 2025:KER:66565 1. Open wound on plantar aspect of right foot.
2. Amputation of 3rd toe at PIP joint with exposed PPX bone right leg.
3. Multiple lacerated wounds in the 1st web space sole of foot and dorsum of foot.
Considering the fact that there was an amputation of the 3rd toe of the right foot, I find that a period of three months can be taken for awarding compensation under the afore head.

Since the monthly income is refixed at 12,000/-, the total compensation payable under the head is recalculated thus:
36,000/- (12,000x3).
The tribunal has already awarded an amount of 14,000/- under the said head.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 22,000/- under the head loss of earnings.
Permanent Disability :- The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that, as per Ext.A7 disability certificate, the disability was assessed at 6.2%.

However, the Tribunal reduced the same to 3%, by applying the provisions relating to disability compensation under the Employees'
Compensation Act and fixed the percentage at 3%.
The appellant was a physical education teacher and Ext.A13 series documents also reveals that pursuant to the accident he obtained Degree in Physical Education.
It is true that the disability certificate was issued by a single doctor and that the MACA NO. 3397 OF 2017 2025:KER:66565 said doctor was not examined.

However, if the Tribunal had any doubt, it ought to have referred the appellant for further examination to the State Medical Board, as held by the apex court in Rajkumar v. Ajay Kumar [2011 (1) KLT 620 SC] and by this court in Manikantan G. v. K.Janardhanan Nair [2021(5) KHC 305] and hence the reasoning of the tribunal does not appear to be acceptable.

sentences.text: Considering the fact that the appellant was a graduate in Physical Education, I find that the percentage of disability shown in Ext.A7 certificate can be accepted and refixed at 6.2%.

Since the monthly income has been refixed as 12,000/-, following the judgments in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi [2017(4) KLT 662(SC)] and Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [2010(2) KLT 802(SC)], the award for the afore head is recalculated as 1,51,776/-
(12,000x12x17x6.2/100).

sentences.text: Since, the tribunal has awarded an amount of 30,600/-, there will be an additional amount of 1,21,176/- under the afore head.

Pain and suffering :- The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that though an amount of 1,00,000/- was claimed towards pain and sufferings, the tribunal has awarded only an MACA NO.
3397 OF 2017 2025:KER:66565 amount of 20,000/-.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained as well as the age of the appellant, I find that a total amount of 40,000/- can be awarded under the said head.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 20,000/- under the afore head.

Loss of amenities :- The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that though an amount of 50,000/-

sentences.text: Thus, there will be an additional amount of 20,000/- under the afore head.
Attendant expenses :- The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal has awarded only a sum of 1,800/-, calculated @ 300/- for a period of six days, under the afore head.
Considering the fact that the accident occurred in the year 2014, I am inclined to grant compensation @ 350/- per day for a period of six days.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to get a total sum of 2,100/- (350x6) under the afore head.
The tribunal has already awarded an amount of 1,800/- under the said head.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 300/- under the MACA NO. 3397 OF 2017 2025:KER:66565 head bystander expenses.
Extra nourishment :-
Though an amount of 15,000/- was claimed by the appellant towards the afore head, the tribunal had granted only an amount of 1,000/-.

Considering the year of accident as well as the period of hospitalisation, I am inclined to grant a consolidated sum of 2,000/-
towards extra nourishment.
The tribunal has already awarded an amount of 1,000/- under the said head.
Thus there will be an additional amount of 1,000/- under the afore head.

6. Though the appellant claimed enhancement of compensation under the other heads, on a perusal of the records available, I am not inclined to interfere with the compensation awarded by the tribunal under other heads since it appears to be just and reasonable.

Since the appeal is of the year 2017, I find it appropriate to fix the interest @8% per annum on the enhanced amount.
7.

Thus, the impugned award of the tribunal is modified as follows:-

sentences.text: Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part and the appellant/claimant is awarded an additional compensation of 1,84,476/- (Rupees one lakh eighty four thousand four hundred and seventy six only) over and above the compensation awarded by the tribunal with interest @8% per annum from the date of petition till realization and proportionate costs.

The respondent MACA NO. 3397 OF 2017 2025:KER:66565 insurer shall deposit the said amount together with interest and costs within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

The claimant shall furnish copies of the PAN Card, ADHAAR Card and bank details before the respondent insurer within a period of one month so as to enable the insurance company to make the deposit as ordered above.
In case of failure to furnish details as above, it shall be open for the insurance company to deposit the said amount before the tribunal.
Upon such deposit being made, the entire amount shall be disbursed to the appellant at the earliest in accordance with law.
